checked_arguments: For at least nine heavy residues, the missing heavy-difference set contains no complete nonzero binary plane, since otherwise at most eight plane cosets can contain a heavy residue.
Every missing direction needs ceil(16/P) active light incidences; a weight-two fibre contributes at most one and a weight-three fibre at most two across the missing set.
The exact inequality r*missing_count <= L2+2*L3 is equivalent to r*missing_count+heavy_count+not_weight3_count <= 2*support_size.

The support13/max<=13 and support14/max<=11 consequences follow from the elementary eight- and nine-point difference bounds, the scalar light budget, and the incidence inequality; they do not need a total-weight bound.
Exactly-one spectrum selectors define heavy and weight-three flags by equivalence; heavy-edge AND, covered-direction OR, and missing-direction negation are exact.
The at-least-nine-heavy budget gate and the unary-counter indices impose the stated weighted bound. Repeated input literals count occurrences and implement integer coefficients.
Scope-specific cuts enforce at least ten heavy fibres, at most two missing heavy directions, and complete difference coverage when the number of remaining light vertices is below ceil(16/P).

Optional exactly-ten-heavy propagation correctly forces all light endpoints onto active heavy-light edges, imposes the residual heavy pair lower bound, and forces all light fibres to have weight three when there are two missing directions.

The convenience encoder accepts only S13/exact12, S13/exact13 and S14/exact11 with total upper bound93 and the distinguished residue0 at the exact maximum. It composes the frozen baseline, separately frozen tetrahedral capacity extension, and new incidence cuts.
